name: Question 7
problem: Consider the portion of the surface $z=x+{y}^{3}$ whose projection onto the $xy$-plane is bounded by $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=1.$ Find a repeated integral expression for the surface area of this surface.
worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $z=f(x,y)$ with $(x,y)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
z=x+{y}^{3},\,(x,y)\in D
$$

where the region $D$ is given by

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 1},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066535/assets/87845c65dba220978ca81bd5a2b27816ca15f951cd14d8fe499ab43d3c64ef77.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+{y}^{3})=1, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+{y}^{3})=3{y}^{2},\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂z}{∂x})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂z}{∂y})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+(1)^{2}+{(3{y}^{2})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{2+9{y}^{4}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{1}\sqrt{2+9{y}^{4}}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
